about: Every round of AI agents using Cover as real users and agents would, on the live server: who they were, what blocked them, what they found wrong or confusing, and what was fixed after.

rounds.title: A person's own AI agent uses Cover: a trip, a tight budget, and a red-team agent
rounds.setup: Three Sonnet agents on the live server (localhost:8800, PayPal sandbox), each with only an agent token and /llms.txt. Maya's agent insures a Tokyo trip for two under $150 and simulates a late flight; Leo's agent works under a $30 limit with no autopay; Rin's agent is a security tester checking Cover's guardrails.

testers.name: Maya's agent
testers.role: insure a trip for two, under $150, medical if reasonable

testers.name: Leo's agent
testers.role: a weekend trip within a $30 limit, plus a renters price

testers.name: Rin's agent
testers.role: red team: known disruptions, limits, payout address, injected claim text, others' ids

rounds.outcome: Every guardrail held: an already-delayed flight was refused (TR-3.1), the agent couldn't raise its limit or change where money goes, an over-limit purchase was refused, the injected claim stalled for evidence, and others' ids were refused. Rin's trip paid $100 by PayPal Payouts about a second after AM410 was reported 2.5 hours late. Maya's agent stopped rather than overspend: medical cover costs more than her $150.
fixes: insure_trip no longer needs the oldest traveler's age for flight-only cover, and accepts its arguments wrapped as { answers } too
Flights may name their airports (from, to); otherwise they are still drawn from the flight number
A claim type the policy's plan doesn't include is refused up front with its clause, and flight claims say they are automatic
Trip premiums now count toward the person's monthly spending limit, and the limit message says so
The product list in errors includes travel; /llms.txt documents the demo controls as demo-only

rounds.title: Giving to several causes, a neighborhood fund, and a seller's agent selling Cover at checkout
rounds.setup: Three Sonnet agents on the live server (PayPal sandbox). Jordan's agent splits his giveback and looks into a neighborhood fund (three neighbors at his ZIP already on Cover); Priya's agent insures a three-person trip to Lisbon with medical, splits the giveback and cancels the outbound flight with the demo feed; Northwind Trips' checkout agent, with only a partner key and /llms.txt, tries to embed Cover in a customer's checkout.

testers.name: Jordan's agent
testers.role: split the giveback; find and join the neighborhood fund

testers.name: Priya's agent
testers.role: insure a group trip with medical; a cancelled flight

testers.name: Northwind's checkout agent
testers.role: a seller's agent embedding Cover at checkout

rounds.outcome: Jordan's agent set 67/33 causes and joined the 78704 fund on its own (4 households, $12). Priya's agent bought $307.08 of cover for three in one call; cancelling TP236 paid $900 automatically. Northwind's agent stopped rather than invent the oldest traveler's age, so it never reached an offer.
fixes: A seller's offer no longer needs an age: without one it offers flight cover, and a destination in words ("Cancún, Mexico") is read into Cover's region; missing trip fields are named instead of "can't offer this online"
The causes chosen with a purchase become the person's current choice (whoami and giveback_status show the split)
Choosing a cause whose pool is in deficit this year says so

flight_status shows what is left per traveler and for the trip; the cap reads "$600 a traveler ($1,800 for 3)"; payouts say they go to the policyholder for every traveler, and each payout status (UNCLAIMED, RETURNED...) says what it means

The neighborhood fund's monthly amount counts toward the person's limit; joining returns the PayPal id and how to leave; agents can leave, propose and vote (leave_neighborhood_fund, propose_project, vote_project)
